question: Oracle says roughly X% of its RPO at Aug 31, 2026 will be recognized in the next 12 months. What dollar amount does that imply, and how does it compare (as a ratio) to Oracle's trailing-twelve-month total revenue through Q1 FY2027?
grading: Implied 12-month RPO ±1% (USD billions); TTM revenue ±0.5%; ratio ±0.02x; must show TTM build
answer: Approximately 13% of Oracle’s USD 664 billion RPO implies USD 86.32 billion recognized over the next twelve months. TTM total revenue through Q1 FY2027 is USD 71,776 million: FY2026 USD 67,357 million + Q1 FY2027 USD 19,345 million − Q1 FY2026 USD 14,926 million. The implied RPO amount / TTM revenue ratio is 1.2026x. The 13% is approximate and RPO recognition is not total-revenue guidance. [G24-E1, G24-E2]

output.answer:
## The numbers

**Oracle's disclosed conversion rate:** In its Q1 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ended Aug 31, 2026), Oracle states RPO was **$664 billion**, "of which we expect to recognize approximately **13%** as revenues over the next twelve months," 37% in months 13–36, 34% in months 37–60, and the remainder thereafter. (This ticked up from 12% at FY2026 year-end.) ([SEC 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1341439/000119312526389274/orcl-20260831.htm))

**Implied dollar amount:** 13% × $664B ≈ **$86 billion** of RPO expected to be recognized as revenue over the next 12 months.

**Trailing-twelve-month revenue through Q1 FY2027:** Q1 FY27 revenue was $19.345B, and it replaces Q1 FY26's $14.926B in the trailing window. So:

| Component | Amount |
|---|---|
| FY2026 total revenue | $67.357B |
| Less Q1 FY26 (Aug 31, 2025) | −$14.926B |
| Plus Q1 FY27 (Aug 31, 2026) | +$19.345B |
| **TTM revenue through Q1 FY27** | **≈ $71.8B** |

## The ratio

$86B ÷ $71.8B ≈ **1.2x**

So the portion of Oracle's $664B backlog it expects to recognize in the next 12 months is roughly **120% of its trailing-twelve-month total revenue** — i.e., about 1.2 years' worth of current revenue is already contracted and scheduled to convert within the coming year. That's a striking figure for a company whose backlog is largely long-dated AI cloud contracts, and it helps explain the gap between 13% near-term conversion and the ~34% revenue growth Oracle guides to for FY2027 (since only ~$86B of the $664B lands in the next 12 months, most of the growth must come from that slice plus new bookings converting).

**Caveats:**
- The 13% is management's estimate and has historically been conservative; it was 10% a year ago.
- RPO recognition ≠ booked revenue timing precisely; some RPO is billed but unrecognized deferred revenue, and contract timing can shift.
- If you use the FY26 year-end figure (12% of $638B = ~$77B), the ratio would be about **1.07x** instead.

Sources: [Oracle Q1 FY27 earnings release](https://www.oracle.com/news/announcement/q1fy27-earnings-release-2026-09-10), [Oracle 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1341439/000119312526389274/orcl-20260831.htm), [Oracle FY2026 results](https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Oracle-Announces-Record-Q4-and-FY-2026-Results-Driven-by-Cloud-Infrastructure--Cloud-Applications/default.aspx).
